ca_campfire_crag_north_face.blurb: The steeper, shadier side of Campfire Crag, in the Indian Cove part of Joshua Tree, a short stroll from the road. Nearly all of the 19 climbs are trad, with just a couple of bolted lines. The grades split into two camps: a handful of easy and moderate routes from about 5.6 to 5.9, then a harder group in the 5.11s and 5.12s. The stone here is darker and generally better than on the opposite face, though a few routes are weak. Because the wall stays out of the sun for most of the day, it suits warm weather, and it sees far fewer climbers than the busy walls nearby.

ca_mount_san_antonio_mt_baldy.blurb: Mount San Antonio, better known as Baldy, is the tallest summit in the San Gabriel Mountains, and this page covers its winter climbing above Mount Baldy Road in the Angeles National Forest. Of the 19 routes, most are snow and ice lines, mainly from WI1 to WI3, with a handful of mountaineering routes graded Class 3 and 4, plus a few short trad and top-rope climbs up to about 5.9. Baldy Bowl is the big snow slope that draws mountaineers, with steepness around 45 to 50 degrees. Expect things to depend on the snow year: the bowl is loose scree when it is bare.

ca_ranger_station_rock.blurb: A single-pitch trad crag high above the Lost Horse ranger station in Joshua Tree, near Twentynine Palms. Nearly all of the 19 climbs are trad, plus one top-rope line. The mix is friendly: a good number of routes between 5.4 and 5.8, then a solid group in the 5.10s and one at 5.11. Cracks and faces both show up, and a standard Joshua Tree rack covers most of it. Wear approach shoes, since the hike up goes through a boulder field and the terrain is loose and sandy. It is a quieter option than the better-known walls in the area.
ca_ranger_station_rock.parking_note: Leave the car at the final pullout on Lost Horse Road, the same spot used by the nearby Atlantis and Super Heroes climbs.
ca_ranger_station_rock.approach: Follow the dirt road on foot to the ranger station, pass around the right side of the building, then pick up a use trail climbing through the boulder field to the rock.

ca_45_wall.blurb: A compact sport wall on the limestone ridge of the Siskiyou-area Lover's Leap, above Scott Valley in far northern California. All 19 routes are bolted, and nearly every one falls between 5.9 and 5.11, with the heart of it in the 5.10s and a single 5.12. Climbs are short to medium in length, on very solid rock, and the wall gets sun for most of the day, so plan around the heat. Doesn't Suck, a 5.9, and the 5.10 Finger Bucket are the most-rated lines. Reach it by following the main trail up to the saddle between the big formation and a smaller one, then turning right.

ca_boney_bluff.blurb: A steep sport cliff in the Santa Monica Mountains with ocean views, known for fingery, powerful pocket pulling on strongly overhanging rock. All 19 routes are bolted, short at about 30 to 50 feet, and sustained. This is a crag for strong climbers: one 5.10, a few 5.11s, then a clear majority at 5.12 and 5.13, with one 5.14. Many link-ups are possible and the bolting is good. It is widely regarded as one of the better training walls in Southern California. The hike in is long, and the return can run past dark, so bring a headlamp.

ca_juniper_wall.blurb: A crack-focused wall in the Rock Creek canyon of the Eastern Sierra, around 9,000 feet, just right of Saguaro Wall. Most of the 19 climbs are trad, with a few bolted lines, and the sweet spot is 5.9 to 5.10, including a good number of 5.10s and a few 5.11s and 5.12s plus an easy route. The rock was cleaned thoroughly, and there are anchors midway and on top, which allows lowering or top-roping. Facing southeast, it catches plenty of sun, so the season stretches from early spring to fall, with shade arriving in summer afternoons.

ca_beak_boulder_area.blurb: A cluster of boulders in the Loveland section of Joshua Tree, in the Pinto Basin, facing Vector Rock. Its 19 routes are a split of trad (10) and bolted (9). Grades run from an easy 5.3 up to the 5.12 range, though most land between 5.8 and 5.10. Totally Tubular and Bath Water are among the better-known easier lines, while Throbbing Gristle is the standout hard route. The route finding involves scrambling up behind the boulder, and a few spots call for tunneling through gaps. Expect a long, remote desert walk rather than a roadside crag.
ca_beak_boulder_area.parking_note: Start from the Split Rock parking area, the same trailhead used for Tiger Rocks and Vector Rock.

ca_al_s_garage.blurb: A quiet volcanic cliff north of Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at about 7,600 feet near Big Springs. A rock tower in the middle splits the wall in two. Of the 19 routes, most are bolted, with a few trad lines. Grades are moderate and fair: a few 5.8s, several 5.9s, and a bulk of 5.10s, with one 5.11. Routes are roughly 50 to 60 feet, so a typical sport rack and quickdraws will do. Facing southwest, the cliff is shaded early and warms later in the day, and spring and fall are the best times. The long, rough drive keeps crowds away.
ca_al_s_garage.parking_note: From US-395 north of Mammoth Lakes, turn onto Owens River Road, pass Big Springs Campground, then follow rough forest roads past a small meadow to the road's end; a high-clearance vehicle helps.
